title: Telemetry‑Driven Auto‑repair Decisionlet and Dry‑Run Harness
creator: Aisha Campos
description: Implement a compact decisionlet service that converts telemetry signatures into safe, confidence‑scored repairlet proposals and can optionally execute them in a gated dry‑run sandbox. Motivation: reduce mean time to repair for common infra/support classes (e.g., hung inference workers, stuck autoscale actions, prefix cache invalidation) by surfacing high‑precision remediation steps while preserving auditability, RBAC gating, and manual override. This ticket implements the core rule engine, a dry‑run worker that replays remediation in an ephemeral sandbox, integration points to Console for review/canary execution, and the audit/provenance exports for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Decisionlet service ingests telemetry signatures and returns top 3 repairlet proposals with confidence scores (0.0-1.0)
Dry‑run harness can execute repairlets against a sandbox cluster with deterministic toggles; results are recorded in the audit log and surfaced in Console
Safety gates: every automated action must pass an RBAC policy check; actions with confidence < 0.85 require manual approval
End-to-end smoke test exists that injects synthetic signature and validates a successful dry run and a real-run rollback path
Telemetry -> decisionlet latency under 250ms for proposal generation at 95th percentile
Metrics and traces instrumented (proposal_count, proposal_confidence_histogram, dryrun_success_rate, dryrun_duration_ms)
Docs: Console review UX spec and runbook templates published in Confluence; implementation PR and runbook link included in ticket
tasks: Design rule schema and signature matcher (Rust) - data model + unit tests
Implement decisionlet API (gRPC + REST shim) and proposal scoring logic
Build dry‑run worker that provisions ephemeral cluster namespace and replays repairlet steps
Integrate RBAC checks and KMS secret fetch for privileged step execution
Console UI: review pane with proposals, confidence, simulated outcome and one‑click canary
Instrument metrics/tracing and add alerting for dry‑run failure rate > 5%
Create synthetic test harness and CI job to run deterministic dry runs on PRs
Write runbook templates and Confluence doc for SREs/first‑line support
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Campos: Created ticket — initial scoping and high-level success criteria. Raised need for RBAC and auditlog early to align with privacy/compliance teams.

2025-02-12 Jun Park: Spiked a Rust matcher prototype; simple LSH+cosine matcher gives high recall on historical signatures. Performance looks promising in dev (p95 120ms). Will push prototype branch today.
2025-02-14 Morgan Lee (SRE): Suggested adding a synthetic failure harness to validate dry‑run fidelity. Also requested a safe rollback token mechanism to revoke any accidental side effects.

2025-02-16 Security review request filed: sec-review-789. Initial note: privileged steps must pull secrets via KMS and the worker must run in a customer‑isolated service account. Security review flagged a need for additional key rotation docs.

2025-02-18 Jun Park: Implemented proposal scoring and confidence thresholding. Added a feature flag (decisionlet.autorepair.enabled) and an internal whitelist for low-risk repairlets. WIP PR opened (see links).
notes: Design decisions: (1) scoring = logistic model over telemetry features + rule heuristics to maintain interpretability; (2) dry‑run will run in a namespaced dev cluster with deterministic seed data to allow reproducible results; (3) all executed steps are recorded to the auditlog with provenance id and optional snapshot of pre-state. Rollout plan: start with proposal‑only mode in Cycle 48, then gated canary execution for infra team, finally enable autorepair for low‑risk classes after two weeks of monitoring. Post‑launch followups: integrate with incident-synthesis assistant to allow automatic postmortem drafts and link to runbook-curation pipeline.
